title: 07 Matrices: Visual Guide
outline: 1. From Vectors To Matrices | the vector addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication you already know, run again on a whole matrix, with a 2x2 to 2x3 shape switch that breaks the sum | matrix arithmetic is entrywise vector arithmetic column by column, so addition and subtraction need identical dimensions while scaling works on any shape

2. Rows Meet Columns | a shape lab where m x n times q x p is declared defined or undefined, plus a real product whose entries you tap to see which row met which column | entry (i,j) of AB is the dot product of row i of A with column j of B, so AB exists only when the column count of A equals the row count of B and the product is m x p

3. AB Versus BA | three pairs of matrices tested against commutativity, associativity, distributivity and the identity, with the two sides computed side by side | commutativity is the property that generally fails while associativity, distributivity and an identity always hold, and a pair that happens to commute proves nothing

4. Solve By Inverse | draggable coefficients for a two-equation system, showing the determinant, the inverse, the solution and both equations drawn as lines | AX = B is solved by left-multiplying by A inverse because A inverse times A is the identity, and det = ad - bc being zero means the lines never cross uniquely so no inverse exists

5. Moving The Plane | identity, scale by 2, reflect across the x-axis, swap coordinates and a live rotation angle applied to the unit square and a test vector | a 2x2 matrix is a linear transformation of the plane whose columns are the images of <1,0> and <0,1>, so every standard transformation can be read straight off the entries
